headline: 10 dead as 29 Bangladeshis drift to Egypt after 10 days at sea
summary: Migrants were heading to Greece from Libya when their boat ran out of fuel and lost its way in the Mediterranean Sea.
details: Twenty-nine Bangladeshi migrants were rescued from a rubber boat and are currently receiving treatment at a hospital in Marsa Matruh, Egypt, according to the Bangladesh Embassy in Cairo.

The group had set sail from Tobruk, Libya, heading for Greece with the help of human traffickers. However, the boat lost its way after running out of fuel, leaving the passengers drifting for approximately 10 days.
A survivor, Abdul Karim, told the embassy that 42 people—including 38 Bangladeshis and 4 Sudanese nationals—started the journey on August 3.
Due to extreme heat, lack of food, and water scarcity, 10 people (9 Bangladeshis and 1 Sudanese) died while drifting in the Mediterranean.
The survivors were forced to dump the bodies of the deceased into the sea as the corpses began to decompose.
The boat eventually reached the coast of Marsa Matruh on August 13, where local police rescued the survivors, 18 of whom were found unconscious or seriously ill.
The Bangladesh Embassy is coordinating with local authorities to provide consular assistance and plans to repatriate the survivors once they are medically fit.
caption:
10 dead, 10 days drifting in the Mediterranean. A harrowing journey from Libya to Greece ends in tragedy in Egypt.

Twenty-nine Bangladeshi migrants were rescued from a rubber boat and are currently receiving treatment at a hospital in Marsa Matruh, Egypt, according to the Bangladesh Embassy in Cairo.

The group had set sail from Tobruk, Libya, heading for Greece with the help of human traffickers. However, the boat lost its way after running out of fuel, leaving the passengers drifting for approximately 10 days.

A survivor, Abdul Karim, told the embassy that 42 people—including 38 Bangladeshis and 4 Sudanese nationals—started the journey on August 3.

Due to extreme heat, lack of food, and water scarcity, 10 people (9 Bangladeshis and 1 Sudanese) died while drifting in the Mediterranean.

The survivors were forced to dump the bodies of the deceased into the sea as the corpses began to decompose.

The boat eventually reached the coast of Marsa Matruh on August 13, where local police rescued the survivors, 18 of whom were found unconscious or seriously ill.

The Bangladesh Embassy is coordinating with local authorities to provide consular assistance and plans to repatriate the survivors once they are medically fit.

headline_marked: 2 hand grenades found: [[Neo-JMB associate arrested]] in Dhaka
headline: 2 hand grenades found: Neo-JMB associate arrested in Dhaka
summary: Jewel Bhuiyan, a former prison escapee and associate of bomb-maker 'Bommaru Mamun', was caught in Demra with explosives.
details: Police and the Anti Terrorism Unit (ATU) arrested Jewel Bhuiyan, alias 'Ostad', during a joint operation in the Sarulia area of Demra, Dhaka.
During the search, security forces recovered two hand-grenade-like objects from his possession.
Law enforcement agencies identify Jewel as a close associate of Nazmul Hasan Mamun, a notorious bomb-maker for Neo-JMB known as 'Bommaru Mamun'.
Jewel was previously a member of Hizbut Tahrir and later developed ties with Mamun while in prison, reportedly collaborating after being released on bail.
The suspect has a history of prison escapes; he fled Narsingdi District Jail on July 19, 2024, was recaptured on July 25, and was later released on bail in September.
Another suspect, identified as Arif Chowdhury, was also detained from the scene during the operation.
caption:
A Neo-JMB associate and former prison escapee has been arrested in Dhaka with two hand grenades.

Police and the Anti Terrorism Unit (ATU) arrested Jewel Bhuiyan, alias 'Ostad', during a joint operation in the Sarulia area of Demra, Dhaka.

During the search, security forces recovered two hand-grenade-like objects from his possession.

Law enforcement agencies identify Jewel as a close associate of Nazmul Hasan Mamun, a notorious bomb-maker for Neo-JMB known as 'Bommaru Mamun'.

Jewel was previously a member of Hizbut Tahrir and later developed ties with Mamun while in prison, reportedly collaborating after being released on bail.

The suspect has a history of prison escapes; he fled Narsingdi District Jail on July 19, 2024, was recaptured on July 25, and was later released on bail in September.

Another suspect, identified as Arif Chowdhury, was also detained from the scene during the operation.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #Security #CounterTerrorism #News

Source: Jamuna TV, Somoy News
